The oracle PAR2 files were generated by par2cmdline-turbo 1.5.0 (macOS arm64):

    par2 c -q -s4096 -c4 -n1 oracle.par2 alpha.bin beta.bin empty.bin

Original, deterministic source files: alpha.bin is 17411 bytes; beta.bin is
9017 bytes; empty.bin is empty (the oracle tool excludes it). Byte i is
`byte((i*73) ^ (i>>3) ^ sum(UTF8(filename)))`. Tests regenerate these bytes.
The fixture tests Ether against an independent implementation, including
protected-file ordering, GF16 constants, exponents and final-slice padding.
No external media or credentials are included.

The streaming fixtures use a 131123-byte `repair.mkv` consisting of
`byte((i*73) ^ (i>>3) ^ 41)`, with its first four bytes replaced by
`1a 45 df a3`. This is synthetic data, not playable media.

    par2 c -q -s16384 -c4 -n1 stream.par2 repair.mkv
    par2 c -q -s4096 -c16 -n1 wide.par2 repair.mkv

They exercise article/slice boundary mismatches and an article spanning more
than four missing slices. Only independently generated PAR2 files are stored.
